ink-black.$description: Ink Black — Body text, button fills, hairline borders, slider tracks, active states — the single dominant tone that gives every specimen its anchor

paper-white.$description: Paper White — Page canvas, card surfaces, input fills, button text on dark fills

foam-gray.$description: Foam Gray — Subtle surface lift and low-contrast dividers when a row needs to separate from pure white without using ink

concrete-gray.$description: Concrete Gray — Medium-contrast borders, control outlines, and structural separators.

graphite.$description: Graphite — Secondary surfaces and darker neutral blocks when a row needs more weight than white but less than pure black

mid-ink.$description: Mid Ink — Near-black with a barely-perceptible cool cast — used where pure #000000 would feel flat against the slightly warm page

ash.$description: Ash — Quiet link text and low-emphasis labels

sterlingvf.$description: Workhorse for all UI chrome: navigation, labels, slider values, button text, font metadata, links. The weight 300 is reserved for quiet labels; 400 reads as the default body voice; 500 only appears on active or selected states. A barely-positive tracking (0.017em) at 12–14px gives small caps a calm, typeset quality rather than a screen-reading feel.

sterling.$description: Static fallback face for the same UI roles as SterlingVF, used where variable axes aren't needed (icons, simple buttons). Carries a slightly wider tracking than the variable sibling to stay legible at very small sizes.

formative.$description: Showcase serif. Drawn at 158px as the hero specimen, its tight -0.02em tracking and unit line-height let the letterforms touch shoulder-to-shoulder — a wall of type, not a line of type.

voyager.$description: Showcase display face. The -0.10em tracking is the design's most extreme optical choice — letters collapse into each other at 158px to form a continuous black bar, a deliberate counterpoint to the breathable Sterling UI text.

blokvf.$description: Geometric display specimen. Uses normal letter-spacing — the only showcase face that doesn't pull tight — because its blocky geometry already has built-in density.

arbeitprocontrastvf.$description: High-contrast serif specimen, shown in the hero photograph as a printed type-on-monitor mockup — the only showcase face presented through photography rather than as raw type on the page.

anthrovf.$description: Humanist sans specimen at display scale, pairing weight 400 and tight tracking to show a softer counterpoint to Blok's geometry.

apexvf.$description: Display specimen with the loosest line-height of the showcase set, letting ascenders and descenders breathe vertically.

arbeittechnikvf.$description: Technical/industrial specimen, tight tracking and unit line-height so its monoline forms read as a structural element.

work-sans.$description: Failsafe for any environment where the custom Sterling face cannot load — never the primary voice, but the only Google face in the system.
